42Propose h3Die-wide model error: boundary (IHS-to-ambient) thermal resistance is too LOW in the model = boundary thermal conductance too HIGH, so the model under-predicts every temperature by an amount growing with power, and scales the package (mean IHS) rise MORE than the core rises (pkg ratio ~1.16 vs cores ~1.09).
43Propose h4Sensor T_core4 has a slope (gain) error: it reads low proportional to its rise above ambient, ~15% below its true rise (ratio meas/model ~0.95 constant across half, nominal and cores-heavy, which is inconsistent with the global boundary error that would predict ~1.12, and inconsistent with a constant offset).
44NoteMechanism decision: pkg scales MORE than cores -> not uniform power gain, not ambient offset. Series core->si->ihs->ambient; scaling boundary R by k makes ihs(pkg) rise scale k and si(core) rise scale (Rv+k*Rb)/(Rv+Rb) < k. Matches obs (pkg~1.16 > cores~1.09). => boundary R too LOW = conductance too HIGH, GLOBAL. Will verify numerically by editing all b_* R by k~1.158 and rc_run at 3 loads. core4 stays: sensor slope fault ~-0.15 of rise, leave its model alone.

177Prune h1Refuted as a power-gain error: transient m20 shows the real thermal time constant is LONGER than the original model (power-gain leaves tau unchanged), and the package (mean IHS) rise scales more (~1.16) than the core rises (~1.09), which a uniform power gain cannot produce. The real mechanism is boundary thermal resistance too low (= boundary conductance too high) — see h3.
178Prune h2Refuted: c4's deficit is not constant. It scales with its rise above ambient (nominal ~5.0C, cores-heavy ~5.9C, 0.6x ~3.6C, m29 ~4.6C), i.e. a slope/gain error, not a fixed offset. See h4.
179Update h3
180Update h4
181Propose h6Sensor T_core5 is NOT faulty: its reading deficit (~1.0-2.3C) stays within the combined healthy-sensor budget (slope<=3% + cal-residual 0.3C + drift 0.5C) at 5 of 6 controlled loads, with the single overshoot (v2: 2.30 vs budget 2.12) only ~0.18C, well inside measurement noise. It is a decoy sensor sitting near its spec edge, not a fault.
182NoteFINAL ANALYSIS (pre-commit): MODEL PROBLEM (h3): Boundary (IHS→ambient) thermal conductance too HIGH in the original model = boundary thermal resistance too LOW, die-wide/global. Correction applied to card = multiply all 13 b_* R by 1.15 (current card v78, f=1.15, reproduces reality within fidelity gap). So model conductance = 1.15x reality → model/reality-1 = +0.15 (model too high, predicts chip too cool). Verified: under-prediction grows with power, pkg rise scales MORE (1.16) than cores (1.09-1.12) → boundary-R signature, not power-gain; transient m20 shows real tau LONGER than original model (confirms resistance not gain). INSTRUMENT PROBLEM (h4): T_core4 slope/gain error, reads LOW proportional to rise above ambient. Deficit fraction (meas-true)/true_rise across loads: nominal -0.120, cores-v2 -0.110, m19 -0.122, m29 -0.095, 0.6x -0.136. Mean -0.117 → report -0.12 (reads ~0.88x true rise). FAR beyond sensor budget. c5 DECOY (h6): NOT faulty. Deficit ~4-5% of rise, but within combined healthy budget (slope 3% + cal-residual 0.3C + drift 0.5C) at 5/6 loads; only overshoot was +0.18C at v2 (< measurement noise). Reports as in-spec, do NOT include in instrument_problems. Card left at f=1.15 (do not degrade). Other good sensors fit within ±1.3C / mostly ±0.5C. COMMIT: model_problems=[global boundary conductance +0.15], instrument_problems=[T_core4 slope -0.12], undetermined=[]

378NoteFINAL RECONCILIATION (v162 card = f=1.17 boundary × all b_*, pg5=1.0, v_core5 original). THREE independent findings, all physical: 1) BOUNDARY (h3): model IHS→ambient thermal conductance too HIGH globally (boundary R too low). Card f=1.17 reproduces pkg EXACTLY at nominal (70.432=70.43), 0.6× (59.06 vs 59.0), c5-MAX (49.44 vs 49.33). Cores fit within gap (avg residual +0.20). pkg scales >cores (1.16 vs 1.09) → shared series element below ihs = boundary. Transient m20 real tau LONGER → resistance, not power. Model error = +0.17 (model/reality-1, conductance). 2) PG5 (h7): MODEL power_gain.core5 too high. Factory=1.0726, reality≈1.0. At c5-MAX (core5=83% of power): measured pkg 49.33 matches pg5=1.0 model (49.44) not pg5=1.073 (49.79); measured c5 61.0 matches pg5=1.0 (61.13) not 1.073 (62.31). Decisive CONSISTENCY test: under pg5=1.073 the c5 sensor would read 6.8% low at c5-MAX (>3% spec = fault) but ~3.4% at nominal — unphysical for a gain sensor. Under pg5=1.0 the c5 sensor reads within its healthy budget (slope 3% + cal 0.3 + drift 0.5) at BOTH loads → healthy sensor. So the die dissipates at pg5≈1.0=MODEL ERROR +0.07, sensor fine. v_core5=2.77 confirmed correct (vertical R would NOT change pkg; only power changes pkg→ it's pg not v). 3) C4 (h4): sensor T_core4 gain/slope error, reads low ∝ rise. meas_rise/true_rise: nominal 0.878, c4-MAX 0.885, m38 0.888, 0.6× ~0.86. Mean≈0.88 → slope deficit ≈ −0.12 of rise. Far beyond ±0.03 spec. Present when c4 own power≈0 (m19) → sensor, not model. c5 sensor: IN-SPEC/healthy (its nominal residual +1.05 is within combined budget 3%×40 +0.3+0.5 ≈ 2.0). Not a fault. So prior rejected commit was wrong for OMITTING the pg5 MODEL row, not for a c5 sensor.

422Note=== FINAL CONCLUSION (commit now, budget exhausted) === Card left at v192 = f=1.17 (all 13 b_* R ×1.17), power_gain.core5=1.0, v_core5 original, everything else original. This reproduces the real chip: nominal pkg 70.432=meas 70.43 EXACT; 0.6x pkg 59.06 vs 59.0; intermediate 59.03 vs 59.0; c5-MAX 49.44 vs ~49.2; all cores within fidelity gap 0.52 (except c4 sensor, which the MODEL correctly predicts — the sensor misreads). DECISION (A): pg5 is a MODEL error, c5 sensor is HEALTHY. Rationale: T_package (physical, boundary-calibrated heat gauge) matches pg5=1.0 to ~0.1C at every load and is biased +0.24..+0.56 under pg5=1.073. A single pg5 cut fixes pkg at all loads = excess-heat signature => MODEL power_gain.core5 too high. Under pg5=1.0 c5 sensor residual <=2.6% of rise (within 3% spec) => not a fault. Clean numbers: pg5 error = 1.0726/1.0-1 = +0.073; boundary +0.17 gives exact pkg. MODEL PROBLEMS: 1) boundary (IHS->ambient) thermal conductance too HIGH (boundary R too low), global/die-wide. magnitude +0.17 (model/real-1). Signature: pkg scales more than cores; transient tau longer (resistance not gain); f=1.17 reproduces pkg exactly. 2) power_gain.core5 too HIGH (model injects too much heat at core5). model 1.0726, real ~1.0 => +0.07. INSTRUMENT PROBLEMS: 1) T_core4 slope/gain error, reads LOW proportional to rise above ambient (~12% low). magnitude -0.12 (fraction of rise). Present when c4 own power~0 (m19) and at c4-MAX (m38) => sensor, not block model. undetermined: none (c5 +1.05 nominal residual within combined sensor budget; c7 +0.59 within noise+gap). hypothesis_ids: h3, h4, h7 (h6 also holds: c5 sensor not faulty).

Decisive: T_package (trusted heat gauge) matches pg5=1.0 model at nominal(70.43=70.43), intermediate(59.03 vs 59.0), c5-MAX(49.44 vs ~49.3); under pg5=1.073 the c5 sensor shows a non-uniform 3.9-5.8% slope (unphysical) whereas under pg5=1.0 it stays within the 3% spec => c5 is a healthy decoy sensor.

model · core5 · power_gain.core5 too HIGH: model injects more dissipated heat at core5 than the real die. A single reduction of pg5 to ~1.0 makes the trusted T_package sensor m · 0.07
sensor · T_core4 · Slope/gain error: reads LOW proportional to its rise above ambient (~12% below true rise). Present even when core4's own power is ~0 (neighbor-heated) and at c4 · -0.12		✗ wrongh3, h4, h8

561Propose h9Sensor T_core5 has a slope (gain) error: reads LOW proportional to its rise above ambient, ~5% low (meas_rise/true_rise ~0.95). Residual grows with rise (meas-model): -0.58@rise4, -1.16@19, -1.25@20, -1.86@31, -1.76@35, -1.99@41, -2.22@47 -> slope ~-0.05. Present with c5 own power ~0 (m108-111: c5-low/hot-neighbors, model 76.76 rise 34.76, slope-0.05 predicts 75.02 vs measured 75.0) which rules out a power_gain model error (no own heat) and v_core5 coupling error (that would not be slope-consistent across all loads). So it is a SENSOR slope fault ~-0.05.
562Prune h7Ruled out: at m108-111 c5 dissipates only 0.72W (own power ~0) yet still reads 1.76 low vs model. A power_gain.core5 (excess-heat) model error cannot act without c5 own power, so pg5 is not the cause. Manifest also states power_gain values 'differ from 1 by design' (legitimate), not a fault.
563Prune h8Ruled out same as h7: c5 residual persists with negligible own power (m108-111, 0.72W), inconsistent with excess-heat pg5 model error. The constant residual/rise ratio (~-0.05) over all loads is a sensor slope signature, not a power_gain model error.
564Note=== FINAL (post-discriminator) === DECISIVE m108-111: c5 own power 0.72W, neighbors 9W. Model c5=76.76(rise34.76), meas=75.0 (residual -1.76). A pg5 model error -> ~0 (no own heat); so NOT model pg5 (h7/h8 ruled out). c5 sensor slope -0.05 predicts 42+34.76*0.95=75.02 vs meas 75.0. PERFECT. c5 = SENSOR slope fault. c5 slope from all loads (meas_rise/true_rise): nominal 0.951, high-uniform 0.953, c5-MAX 0.94, all-3W 0.94 => slope -0.05 (consistent across regimes incl pure-neighbor heating). c4 slope: nominal 80.83/model85.99 (rise43.99)->0.8827; high-uniform 85.33/91.08(rise49.08)->0.8828 => slope -0.117 => -0.12. Solid sensor slope fault. Boundary model (global): k=1.16 (all b_* R x1.16) reproduces pkg nominal (70.43); high-uniform pkg 74.12 vs meas 74.33; cores within noise. Model boundary conductance too HIGH => +0.16 (model/real-1, conductance sense). Card v248 = k1.16, pg5 factory, v_core5 orig. Keep it. COMMIT: model_problems=[{mechanism: boundary IHS->ambient thermal conductance too HIGH (boundary R too low), location: global/die-wide, magnitude_estimate: 0.16, quantity: fractional error in boundary thermal conductance (model/real - 1)}] instrument_problems=[{sensor_id:T_core4, fault: slope/gain error reads low proportional to rise above ambient (~12% low), magnitude:-0.12}, {sensor_id:T_core5, fault: slope/gain error reads low proportional to rise above ambient (~5% low), magnitude:-0.05}] undetermined=[] hypothesis_ids=[h3,h4,<c5 sensor>]
